text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Deputy Finance Minister Peter Stanek said the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development and the European Union were strongly pressing on Slovakia to complete privatisation of the banking sector.

- Russian ambassador to Slovakia Sergei Zlotov said his country would not change its negative attitude towards NATO enlargement if Slovak citizens voted in a referendum for membership of the alliance. Zlotov, however, said that this does not mean that the two countries would become enemies.

- Slovakia expects the International Court of Justice in The Hague to confirm its demands for compensation of losses caused by Hungarian withdrawal from the joint dam project on the river Danube. The Slovak-Hungarian law suit over the controversial Gabcikovo dam will start on March 3.

- The opposition Party of Democratic Left (SDL) said it would vote for the second time in favour of the postponement of bank privatisation if the government returns the legislation to parliament for re-assessment.
- The SDL rejected information that its bilateral talks with the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) were aimed at creating room for SDL's entry to the governing coalition.
- The state loans to agricultural sector totalled more than 2.6 billion crowns between September 1994 and December 1996.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Slovak capital Bratislava said it planned to issue a 777 million crown tranche of municipal bonds to cover its this year's budget revenues.

- Management of Druha Obchodna, majority owner of Slovakia's sole oil and gas storage company Nafta Gbely, ruled out any political connections with the ruling parties. Druha Obchodna also rejected rumours that Russian citizens hold an unspecified stake in it.
- The government is considering unspecified relief from fines from delays in loan repayments for troubled, but, what it considers, promising companies.
PRAVDA - Slovakia's largest private television channel TV Markiza said it would submit a bid in the privatisation tender for the second terrestrial channel of the public Slovak Television.

SME - The Slovak opposition parties have completed collecting signatures for a petition initiating direct presidential elections. The opposition, however, said it would only present the petition to the president to call a referendum if the parliament rejects its proposal to change the presidential electoral system by constitutional law.
- The National Property Fund (NPF), the state privatisation agency, said citizens will be able to start exchanging their privatisation bonds for shares from the NPF portfolio in the near future.
